problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.

activity_context.topic_title: Projecting Vectors Onto Subspaces in Euclidean Spaces (Orthogonal Bases)

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
feedback.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{5\cdot 2+1\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 0+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{5\cdot 3+1\cdot 2+3\cdot 1+1\cdot (-2)}{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ 

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}\,x}{‖x‖\,‖{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x‖} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 5+1\cdot 0+3\cdot 1+1\cdot (-1)}{\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{5}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{27}{\sqrt{36}\sqrt{27}} \\  & =\frac{27}{6\cdot 3\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{6},
$$

which is already an acute angle.
